book.old: {t('The piano looks like 88 different keys, but it is one small pattern, repeated: a small house of 2 black keys that carries 3 white keys, and a big house of 3 black keys that carries 4. Learn the pattern, and you always know where you are on the piano. book.new: {t('The piano\'s 88 keys are one small pattern, repeated. A small house: 2 black keys, 3 white keys. A big house: 3 black keys, 4 white keys. book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>검은건반은 집의 지붕이에요. 검은건반 2개 = 작은 집의 지붕, 3개 = 큰 집의 지붕. 작은 집, 큰 집, 작은 집, 큰 집... 피아노 끝까지 같은 두 집이 반복돼요. : <>The black keys are the roofs of the houses. Two black keys = the small house's roof; three = the big house's. Small, big, small, big... the same two houses repeat all the way up the piano.}
book.new: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>검은건반은 집의 지붕이에요. 검은건반 2개 = 작은 집, 3개 = 큰 집. 두 집이 피아노 끝까지 반복돼요. : <>The black keys are the roofs. Two black keys = the small house. Three = the big house. The two houses repeat all the way up the piano.}

book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>거리는 왼쪽에서 오른쪽으로 올라가요: 낮은 소리는 왼쪽 끝, 바다 아래 거북이와 함께 살고, 높은 소리는 오른쪽 끝, 하늘 위 새와 함께 살아요. : <>And the street climbs from left to right: the low sounds live at the left end with the turtle under the sea, the high sounds at the right end with the bird up in the sky.}
book.new: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>거리는 낮은 왼쪽에서 높은 오른쪽으로 올라가요: 바다 아래 거북이에서 하늘 위 새까지. : <>The street climbs from low on the left to high on the right: from the turtle under the sea to the bird up in the sky.}

book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>흰건반은 아무 데나 있는 게 아니라 어느 지붕 아래에 살아요. 작은 지붕 아래에는 흰건반 3개(왼쪽 문, 집 안, 오른쪽 문), 큰 지붕 아래에는 4개가 살아요. 그림의 연한 색이 누가 어느 집 식구인지 보여 줘요. 3 + 4 = 7: 일곱 개가 지나면 거리가 처음부터 반복돼요. : <>A white key is never just anywhere: each one lives under a roof. Under the small roof live 3 white keys (left door, inside, right door); under the big roof live 4. The faint colours in the picture show who belongs to which house. 3 + 4 = 7. After seven, the street starts again.}
book.new: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>흰건반은 모두 지붕 아래 살아요: 작은 지붕 아래 3개(왼쪽 문, 집 안, 오른쪽 문), 큰 지붕 아래 4개. 연한 색이 집마다 식구를 표시해요. 3 + 4 = 7, 그다음 거리가 반복돼요. : <>Each white key lives under a roof: 3 under the small one (left door, inside, right door), 4 under the big one. The faint colours mark each house's keys. 3 + 4 = 7, then the street repeats.}

book.old: <>Move to the big house next door and play its 4 white keys in turn.,
book.new: <>Next door, play the big house's 4 white keys in turn.,

book.old: <>맨 아래부터 맨 위까지 올라가며 소리 내어 말해요: "작은 집... 큰 집... 작은 집..."</>,
book.new: <>맨 아래부터 맨 위까지 소리 내어 말해요: "작은 집... 큰 집... 작은 집..."</>,

book.old: <>Travel from the very bottom to the very top, saying it out loud: "small house... big house... small house..."</>,

book.old: <>작은 집을 찾아 그 흰건반 3개를 차례로 쳐요: 왼쪽 문, 집 안, 오른쪽 문.,
book.new: <>작은 집의 흰건반 3개를 차례로 쳐요: 왼쪽 문, 집 안, 오른쪽 문.,

book.old: <>Find a small house and play its 3 white keys in turn: left door, inside, right door.,
book.new: <>Play a small house's 3 white keys in turn: left door, inside, right door.,

book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>진짜 피아노는 건반 88개, 그래도 작은 집 7채, 큰 집 7채뿐이에요. 4번째 작은 집까지 세면 그 왼쪽 문이 가운데 도(middle C)예요. 가운데 도는 땅이에요: 오른쪽으로 가면 하늘 위로 점점 높이, 왼쪽으로 가면 바다 아래로 점점 깊이 내려가요. : <>A real piano has 88 keys, yet still only 7 small houses and 7 big ones. book.new: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>진짜 피아노는 건반 88개지만, 작은 집 7채와 큰 집 7채뿐이에요. 4번째 작은 집까지 세면 그 왼쪽 문이 가운데 도(middle C)예요. 가운데 도는 땅이에요: 오른쪽은 하늘 위로, 왼쪽은 바다 아래로. : <>A real piano has 88 keys, but only 7 small houses and 7 big ones. book.old: <>맨 아래의 외로운 검은건반을 찾아요: 바닷가에 홀로 선 등대예요. 바로 옆이 가장 낮은 건반이에요.,

book.old: <>가운데 도를 치고, 한 집 아래의 C(바다 속으로)와 한 집 위의 C(하늘로)도 쳐 봐요.,

book.old: {LANG === 'ko' ? <>이제 지도가 보답할 차례예요. 악보 없이도 칠 수 있어요: 검은건반 지붕과 양손의 2, 3, 4번 손가락이면 돼요. 꿀처럼 매끄럽게(레가토): 바통 터치하듯, 다음 음이 울리는 순간 앞의 손가락이 놓아요. : <>Now the map pays you back. guide.old: The piano looks like 88 different keys, but it is one small pattern, repeated. Learn the pattern first, and you always know where you are on the piano.
guide.new: The piano has 88 keys, but they are one small pattern, repeated. Learn the pattern first, and you always know where you are.

guide.old: The black keys are the roofs of the houses. Two black keys together are the roof of a small house; three are the roof of a big house. Small, big, small, big: the same two houses repeat all the way up the piano. Look for the shapes, not the single keys.
guide.new: The black keys are the roofs of the houses. The same two houses repeat all the way up the piano. Look for the shapes, not the single keys.

guide.old: • Low on the left, high on the right. The street climbs from under the sea, where the turtle swims, up into the sky, where the bird flies.
guide.new: • Low on the left, high on the right. The street climbs from the turtle under the sea to the bird up in the sky.

guide.old: A white key is never just anywhere: each one lives under a roof. Under the small roof live 3 white keys (the left door, the inside and the right door); under the big roof live 4. Three and four make seven, and after seven the street starts again.
guide.new: Each white key lives under a roof: 3 under the small roof (the left door, the inside and the right door), 4 under the big roof. Three and four make seven, then the street repeats.

guide.old: This grouping is the key idea of the chapter. A student who sees it finds every note name from the pattern, instead of counting up from the bottom of the piano.
guide.new: This grouping is the chapter's key idea. A student who sees it finds every note name from the pattern, not by counting up from the bottom.

guide.old: A real piano has 88 keys, 52 white and 36 black, yet it is still only the two houses: 7 small ones and 7 big ones. At the very bottom stands one lonely black key with no house at all: the lighthouse, by the sea.
guide.new: A real piano has 88 keys, 52 white and 36 black, but only 7 small houses and 7 big ones. At the very bottom, one lonely black key has no house: the lighthouse, by the sea.

guide.old: Count the small houses from the bottom up to the 4th one: its left door is middle C. Middle C is the ground: go right and the notes climb up into the sky, higher and higher; go left and they dive down under the sea, lower and lower.
guide.new: Count the small houses from the bottom up to the 4th one: its left door is middle C. Middle C is the ground: right climbs up into the sky, left dives down under the sea.

guide.old: Playing needs no written notes at all: just the black-key roofs and fingers 2, 3 and 4. The right hand plays on the big roof, the left hand's 2 and 3 on the small roof. Fingers 1 and 5 come later, with the C position.
guide.new: No written notes needed: just the black-key roofs and fingers 2, 3 and 4. The right hand plays on the big roof, the left hand's 2 and 3 on the small roof. Fingers 1 and 5 come later, with the C position.

guide.old: Show, don't tell: each one is shown on the keyboard.

The black keys come in groups of two and three, and every white key belongs to one of those groups: three at the group of two, four at the group of three. Once that pattern is seen, every note name can be found from it instead of by counting.
guide.new: The black keys come in groups of two and three. Every white key belongs to one group: three at the group of two, four at the group of three. Once you see this pattern, you find every note name from it, not by counting.

guide.old: Tap a white key and watch its whole house light up, count the houses on all 88 keys, and jam on the black keys with the band.
guide.new: Tap a white key to light up its whole house, count the houses on all 88 keys, and jam on the black keys with the band.
